**Task A (3D/4D spatial reasoning) — src/spatial.rs (additive, existing API unchanged), src/bin/g2_spatial.rs**
- Added `BoxTree<D>` (nearest box, k-NN boxes, boxes intersecting a query box, boxes containing a point), `overlap_pairs_tree`, `GridN<D>` (BFS/A* any dimension with path output + validator), `SpaceTime<S>` (S=3 = x,y,z,t; time-monotone moves, waiting, moving obstacles, move/wait costs, exact layered-DP reference). `KdTree`/`Grid`/`Aabb`/sweep-and-prune were already const-generic so I tested+benchmarked them in 4D.
- Space-time semantics: vertex-conflict obstacles only (no swap check); goal reached = first time standing on it at any t ≤ horizon.
- Correctness (results/g2_spatial.json/.log): 15,179,522 exact comparisons (index AND squared distance, ties, sorted lists, path costs), 0 mismatches, across 2D/3D/4D, 300 seeds, sizes 0–400, degenerate cases (empty, k>n, duplicates, lattice ties, flat axis, touching/zero-extent boxes, inverted ranges). `cargo test --release --lib spatial` = 15 tests (8 new g2_*), all green.
- Speed at n=1e5 uniform vs a FAIR heap-based brute force (I added it because the crate brute sorts all n): kd k-NN10 ~45x (2D/3D), ~20x (4D); box k-NN10 ~230–260x (2D/3D), ~120x (4D); nearest ~63–160x. Overlap pairs n=20,000: tree 14–44x in all D; sweep-and-prune drops to 3.7x in 4D. A* vs BFS 2.3–10.8x; space-time A* vs DP 3–7.5x on reachable instances.
- NEGATIVES: radius query slower than brute at n=1e3 (0.4–0.9x); clustered data w/ empty-space queries kd nearest only 1.6–3.4x; space-time A* ~9x SLOWER than DP on UNREACHABLE instances and allocates dense (cell,t) arrays (~36 MB/call at 3M states); 4D degrades (grid ring walk weakest).
- BUG I found+fixed in Grid (not an API change): `auto_cell` on data flat along one axis returned ~1e-5 cell → `Grid::build` tried to enumerate billions of cells (first degenerate run hung >25 CPU-min; diagnosed from code). Fix: ignore flat axes, cap cells at 16n+1024, ring enumeration visits only the shell, k-NN ring bound uses farthest grid edge. Query results unchanged (exact in both); only degenerate-data speed differs. r3_memory_spatial.json was produced with the old code — unaffected in correctness.

**Task B (existing block-float16 / sparse states) — src/bin/g2_memory_tost.rs**
- Pre-declared TOST: margin ±0.005 success, 95% CI + Holm, equivalent = Holm-TOST p<0.05 AND 95% CI inside margin; CLAIM = equivalent in held-out 31-60 AND confirm 61-90; 5 worlds. Reference f64 routers verified decision-identical to the compact ones by selftest.
- PRIMARY RULE (30+30 seeds): certifies bf16-sr 4/5 worlds, f16 2/5, SPARSE u16/q16 4/5, SPARSE f16/q16 3/5, SPARSE f16/f16 3/5. Every miss is a power problem — point estimate ~0 but CI half-width 0.004–0.011 at n=30 in the 32-agent worlds — not a measured loss.
- POWER EXTENSION (declared in code header AFTER seeing that; fresh seeds 91-250, n=160, same rule, separate column): all 5 headline candidates equivalent within ±0.005 in ALL 5 worlds (bf16-sr worst CI ±0.0010). bf12 fails one big world, bf8 fails both big worlds ⇒ below 16-bit block-float is NOT within noise.
- BYTES: persisted packed file 0.03–0.17x of crate JSON. Family A resident RAM NOT reduced (bf16 368kB vs crate 401kB; f16 longtail 1.43MB vs 1.24MB — larger). Family B (sparse F3 brain) resident heap 0.10–0.39x of crate. State save 2.6x (bf16)–6.6x (f16) slower than serde_json save (one-off); load 2–3x faster.
- LATENCY (select+update, ns/decision): vs the crate routers, every candidate is at least as fast → "not hurt" (f16 borderline 0.93x worst-world). But that is mostly because the compact code is leaner; DECODE COST vs the SAME layout with f64 cells regresses: bf16-sr 5–13%, f16 1.3–2.3x, dense u16/q16 1.4–2.1x, sparse brains 1.1–1.9x (parity only in long-tail world). Absolutes moved ~30% between runs on the shared box — use ratios.
- VERDICT on "memory drops WITHOUT hurting routing/latency": routing SUPPORTED for the 16-bit candidates but only via the fresh-seed extension (not the pre-declared 30+30); bytes SUPPORTED for persisted file + sparse-brain RAM, REFUTED for family-A resident RAM; latency not hurt vs crate but regresses vs same-layout f64 cells.
